title: kb_hook answers a prompt without kb: in at most 200 ms, so a prompt's wait on the hooks drops
goal: In the session-load replay, arm A's synchronous UserPromptSubmit hook _tools/kb_hook.py takes at most 200 ms (median of 3 reps; 438 ms at load about 6 before), its answers to kb:, status: and other prefixed prompts unchanged; the worker measures the figure's run-to-run spread before relying on the bound

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import csv, os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
CASE, BOUND_MS = 'UserPromptSubmit _tools/kb_hook.py', 200
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
B = os.path.join(T, 'bin'); os.mkdir(B)
open(os.path.join(B, 'claude'), 'w').write('#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n')
os.chmod(os.path.join(B, 'claude'), 0o755)
ENV = dict(os.environ, PATH=B + os.pathsep + os.environ['PATH'])
out = os.path.join(T, 'out.csv')
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/benchmarks.py', 'run', 'session-load', '--arms', 'A', '--reps', '3', '--out', out],
                   capture_output=True, text=True, env=ENV, timeout=1800)
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(out, encoding='utf-8'))) if os.path.exists(out) else []
shutil.rmtree(T, ignore_errors=True)
assert p.returncode == 0, ('run session-load exit', p.returncode, p.stderr[-400:])
got = [float(r['value']) for r in rows if r['scenario'] == 'session-load' and r['arm'] == 'A' and r['metric'] == 'sync_ms' and r['case'] == CASE]
assert got, ('no sync_ms row for', CASE)
assert got[0] <= BOUND_MS, (CASE, 'sync_ms', got[0], 'over', BOUND_MS)
